newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BA says focus on American Airlines merger.
newsitem.headline: BA says focus on American Airlines merger.

text.p: The planned merger between British Airways Plc and American Airlines is BA's main focus, taking precedence over all else, BA chairman Colin Marshall said on Thursday.

"All of our attention and focus at BA at the moment is getting the American Airlines alliance done, and therefore anything else is pure speculation at this stage," Marshall told reporters in response to a question about a possible alliance between BA and Japan Air System Co Ltd.
American Airlines is a unit of AMR Corp.
But once the BA-American Airlines merger was completed, BA "can start thinking about other possibilities and entering into discussions with other parties that may be interested", Marshall said.
Marshall also said BA hoped that plans for Air China to offer non-stop Hong Kong to London service from next month, its first step into the British market, would help BA win access to Shanghai.
"It is obviously our hope that, as a consequence, our desire to operate into Shanghai will get a fairer wind in future," Marshall said.
BA continued to express its "strong wish" to have access to Shanghai, he said.
"The Chinese government has agreed that discussions can take place in this respect and we are hopeful that before too much longer that we will finally get access to Shanghai," he said.
He said BA was currently offering three flights a week to Beijing, so would probably expect to win "two or three services a week (to Shanghai) until the market really builds up".
Founded in 1955, Air China is China's largest and longest-running carrier.
